key_insight: The paper presents an open-source toolkit that automates RHEED control and analysis so AI agents can guide thin-film synthesis in a more autonomous, quantitative way.
engineering_relevance: It lowers the barrier to agentic, reproducible thin-film growth workflows by combining programmable hardware control, shared interfaces, and extensible software for RHEED measurements.
method: Programmable electron-optics control for RHEED on a pulsed laser deposition system
Automated beam alignment, rocking-curve acquisition, and training-free crystallographic azimuthal alignment
Shared GUI and programmatic access via an MCP server plus an adapter interface for new AI analysis and simulation methods
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a demonstration on a pulsed laser deposition system, including an agent-driven example where natural-language requests selected, configured, and executed quantitative analyses.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful integration with specific hardware and robust validation of new community-developed adapters and AI methods before routine autonomous use.
paper_title: An Open-Source Hardware and Software Toolkit to Enable Agentic RHEED-Guided Thin-Film Synthesis
